ratings_why.fun: Each turn asks a readable question, open this Lid for a Spring or keep it shut for Patience, and chains like Tapwell into the Weaver are a joy to set up; the keyword load (Lid, Knock, Spring, Patient, Underneath, opens last) keeps it from an 8.
ratings_why.distinct: 8 because no tribe today changes what the fight starts with: every Lodge unit begins hidden, the scouted board is closed doors marked with Knocks, and Lids in the front row send attacks into your back row on purpose.

points.text: Signora Corkhinge reads as if she gains +4/+4 herself; the builds say the springing unit gets it. Say "that unit gains +4/+4 (in fight)".
Tapwell opens "the biggest friendly unit next to this", which can be an open unit and do nothing. Say "the biggest friendly Lid next to this".

The fantasy lands in play, not just names: knocks on doors, a patient lodge that pays after wins, a Tyler who opens last. Keep the four Knock kinds as the whole vocabulary; a fifth would tip it into unreadable.

Gossamer Jill's Spiderlings start under Lids although the Spring keyword says fight summons come out open. It works as an exception, but a line in Spring ("unless the card says under a Lid") would save a question.
Show who attacks first on the scouting view, since Lids not counting is a big hidden swing a player can't read from the board.

standouts.why: Grit-Lid Purseweb is the whole tribe in one line: wait under the lid, stab whoever walks across.
Tapwell knocking on the doors beside him is the seed's character turned straight into a chain starter.
Slit-Mender stabbing, closing and stabbing again is the purse-web spider exactly, and reads at once.

weakest.why: Ballot Clerk is a generic gold card with a Patient check; the ballot box fantasy (blackballing) doesn't show up in what it does.
Cork-Lid Doorward's re-close plus next-Knock rule takes a second read, and Slit-Mender already does the same job more clearly.
Worshipful Master's replay of every Spring is hard to follow in a fight and harder to animate.

flags.note: Who gains the +4/+4 is ambiguous as written.
With the Past Master and Corkhinge, one replay can double a long cascade; worth the owner's eye.
Mabyn with Diadem on a winning streak squares growth by Patient count; capped by board size but steep.

verdict_why: Two short wording fixes (Corkhinge's "it", Tapwell's target) would make every card read at a glance; the design itself is in a good spot.
